title: Certify v0.11.0: the exact logical error probability of the rotated surface code under a lookup-table decoder — syndrome-space character sums collapse a certified bracket to a single rational
description: Part H of this program (doi:10.5281/zenodo.21895825) published machine-checkable two-sided rational brackets on the logical error probability P_L of the distance-3 and distance-5 rotated surface codes, one round, circuit-level depolarizing noise, under a fixed lookup-table (coset-leader) decoder, and named its own frontier: exact re-verification of the uncorrectable-set counts at weight 7 exceeded a pure-Python checker, because the shipped method enumerated C(77,7) = 2,404,808,340 fault sets. This release removes both the truncation and the wall at d <= 5. A syndrome-space character sum (a MacWilliams-type Walsh-Hadamard argument) yields every uncorrectable count A_w for w = 0..m in a single O(2^n n) pass over the 2^n syndromes, with no per-weight enumeration; its probability-weighted variant yields the EXACT rational P_L, eliminating the bracket altogether. At d = 5 this delivers the previously unreachable A_7 = 832,441,445, the full spectrum through A_77 = 1, the undetectable-logical spectrum re-deriving circuit-level distance 5, and exact rationals for P_L at both published operating points — each lying strictly inside the corresponding Part H bracket, at 0.36 and 0.51 of the bracket widths and never near an endpoint, so the earlier brackets stand as the independent check the exact values passed. A standard-library Python checker re-derives everything from the mechanism list alone in about two minutes at d = 5 within 0.85 GB, and rejects eight classes of tampered certificate. SCOPE, STATED PLAINLY: the result is exact for the independent-mechanism detector error model (Stim's DEM semantics), not the physical depolarizing circuit; it is valid for the stated lookup-table decoder, not a maximum-likelihood or matching decoder; and the trust root is the embedded mechanism list. The honest trade: the C(m,w) enumeration wall is exchanged for a 2^n syndrome-space wall, so one-round distance-7 codes remain out of reach on a laptop by this method, and the note states precisely why. Adversarially reviewed before release; the decision log ships as wedge2-paper/FIXLOG.md. Computations carried out with Claude (Anthropic), directed by the author; Stim used as an untrusted generator only.
